title: Person Tipping Hand Emoji 💁 Meaning: Sass and Hair Flips
description: 💁 was designed as an information desk clerk, but everyone reads it as a sassy hair flip: “duh,” “you’re welcome,” “just saying.” Here is how to use it.
summary: 💁 shows a person holding one hand out, palm up, beside their shoulder. It was created to represent an information desk attendant offering help. In practice it signals sass and confidence, like a hair flip: “obviously,” “you’re welcome,” “just saying.” It can also sincerely mean “here you go” or “FYI.”
meaning: Few emojis have drifted as far from their brief. The Unicode name for 💁 was “Information Desk Person,” and the raised palm was meant to say “how may I help you?” as a clerk at a Japanese department store counter might. Western users saw something else entirely: a woman flipping her hair or balancing an invisible tray of attitude. The sassy reading won.

So today it mostly punctuates statements delivered with a flourish. “I told you it would rain 💁” means “I was right, as usual.” “Not my circus 💁” means “and I don’t care.” It adds a note of self-satisfaction to facts, comebacks and unsolicited advice. The mood is close to 💅 but more talkative, an explanation with a raised eyebrow rather than silent indifference.

The original helpful sense survives in a modest way. People use 💁 to present information (“💁 the link is in the first comment”), to introduce a tip, or to say “at your service.” Customer support accounts and community managers still pick it for that purpose. In those cases the hand is offering something, not flicking hair. Seeing it used this way is a reminder of what the designers had in mind.

Its name was later changed to “Person Tipping Hand,” which describes the pose without settling the debate. The woman version, 💁‍♀️, is the classic sass emoji, while 💁‍♂️ tends to be used either for the same attitude with a wink or for a plainer “there you go.” Whichever version is chosen, the open palm does the talking, presenting a fact, an opinion or a boast for inspection.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use it for smug or cheeky one-liners: stating the obvious, taking credit, or brushing off criticism. It often follows “you’re welcome,” “sorry not sorry,” or “I said what I said.” It can also soften blunt honesty by making it sound performative, as in “that haircut was a choice 💁.”

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: It fits confident captions, clapbacks in comments and “little tip for you” posts. Creators use it when revealing a hack or correcting a misconception, combining the helpful and sassy meanings at once. It has been part of internet diva vocabulary for years, so it can feel slightly retro next to newer favorites such as 💅.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: In its informational sense it is harmless: “💁 reminder that timesheets are due.” The risk is the sassy sense leaking through. Attached to a correction or an “as I mentioned,” it sounds condescending. If you are pointing out something a colleague missed, leave the emoji off. Among work friends who share the joke, it remains a fun way to celebrate small wins.

confusedWith.difference: 💅 is detached and silent, too unbothered to respond. 💁 is the one making the remark, with a hand out as if to say “obviously.” They often appear together.
🤷 lifts both shoulders and hands to mean “I don’t know” or “whatever.” 💁 raises one palm and usually implies the sender knows exactly what they mean.
🙋 stretches an arm overhead to volunteer or ask a question. 💁 keeps the hand at shoulder height, presenting information or attitude instead of asking for a turn.

avoid: Do not attach it to corrections or reminders aimed at coworkers, where it sounds patronizing.
Avoid it when someone is upset with you, since sass reads as refusing to take them seriously.
If you mean to be helpful to a stranger, add clear words so the hand is not taken as sarcasm.
design: A person is shown from the chest up with one hand raised beside the shoulder, palm facing up and tilted outward, generally with a pleasant smile. Vendors vary the shirt color and which hand is raised. The emoji exists as a gender-neutral base, a woman 💁‍♀️ and a man 💁‍♂️, and all accept skin tone modifiers.

faqs.q: What does 💁‍♀️ mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is being sassy, confident or matter-of-fact. It often follows a remark she considers obvious or a moment she is proud of. It is usually playful. If she is giving you information, it may just mean “here you go” with a smile.

faqs.q: What does 💁‍♂️ mean from a guy?
faqs.a: It is typically a cheeky “just saying,” “there it is,” or “you’re welcome.” Guys use it both for joking sass and for neutrally presenting something. It does not carry a romantic meaning in either case.

faqs.q: Why is 💁 called the information desk emoji?
faqs.a: That was its intended meaning. It was designed to depict an attendant at an information counter gesturing politely, and its Unicode name was “Information Desk Person.” The name later changed to “Person Tipping Hand,” reflecting the pose rather than the job.
There is no official hair flip emoji, but 💁 is the one people use for it. The hand position next to the head looks like someone tossing their hair, which is how it became the go-to symbol for sass.
